These paths are mutually exclusive within their own hierarchy but may co-fire at a single timestamp, e.g., a free kick involves both static-ball and pass events. This dual nature necessitates a temporal logic framework where event sets are indexed by time and mapped to a lattice of possible states. The use of frame-accurate annotations implies a discrete-time stochastic process, where each event is a random variable with a probability distribution over its type and attributes. The multimodal aspect introduces cross-modal dependencies through shared timestamps and spatial coordinates. In GSI, this translates into a Bayesian network where video, audio, and positional data contribute independent likelihood terms to infer event types. In GSE, it becomes a dynamic system of state transitions governed by these event primitives, enabling predictive modeling of game flow. The failure mode arises when commercial annotations lack fidelity due to real-time constraints, leading to misalignment with expert annotations—a problem addressed by SCM and NNM metrics.
